requirement: Describe a prospective, nonrandomized, unblinded two-group education study across approximately two to three opioid-treatment clinics, comparing computer-delivered HCV video education with an HCV brochure rather than claiming randomized treatment assignment.

evidence.text: The protocol describes an observational two-group design, video and brochure education, 1:1 matching and two to three participating clinics.

requirement: Define eligibility as adults receiving opioid agonist or replacement therapy who can complete the English-language intervention and assessments, and reconcile whether a current or past HCV history is required before finalizing the analysis population.
acceptable_values: current or past HCV history reconciled

evidence.text: The title and objectives refer to current or past HCV history on opioid replacement therapy; eligibility requires age 18 or older, current Suboxone therapy and English as the primary language.

requirement: Resolve the intervention-label contradiction before unblinding or analysis: protocol page 3 maps Group A to video and Group B to brochure, whereas protocol page 4 reverses those labels; retain a stable participant-level treatment code and do not infer assignment from A/B alone.

evidence.text: Page 3 calls Group A video and Group B brochure, while page 4 calls Group A brochure and Group B video.
The plan labels video as intervention and brochure as control without reconciling the protocol's A/B contradiction.

requirement: Define the primary analysis population and treatment attribution for a nonrandomized study, including consent, baseline assessment, receipt of assigned education, immediate and one-month assessments, clinic transfer, cross-exposure and withdrawal; do not call the population intention-to-treat unless an actual assignment mechanism supports it.

evidence.text: The protocol describes matching, enrollment, two education groups and repeated assessments but supplies no analysis-population or treatment-attribution rule.

requirement: Define one primary HCV-knowledge outcome and contrast, distinguishing change from pre-intervention to immediate post-intervention from retention through one month; do not leave improved literacy, decision-making capacity and percentage retaining knowledge as competing unnamed primary endpoints.

evidence.text: The protocol names improved literacy, decision making and percentage retaining HCV knowledge without a single operational primary endpoint.
The plan mentions pre, post and one-month assessments but only says post and one-month scores will be compared.

requirement: Specify the HCV-knowledge questionnaire version, respondent, item count, correct-answer coding, total-score range, missing-item threshold, direction of improvement and validation procedure before deriving any knowledge score.

evidence.text: The protocol describes a designed pre/post questionnaire and planned reliability and cognitive testing but gives no executable scoring algorithm.

requirement: Map assessments to pre-intervention baseline, immediate post-intervention and one month after education with a plus-or-minus two-week window, and define how out-of-window or telephone assessments are assigned and prioritized.
acceptable_values: one month plus or minus two weeks

evidence.text: The protocol gives pre- and post-intervention assessments.
The plan adds a one-month plus-or-minus-two-week follow-up and permits telephone assessment.

requirement: For the continuous repeated knowledge score, prespecify a complete longitudinal model with education group, categorical visit, group-by-visit interaction, clinic and matching factors, participant-level correlation, covariance structure, degrees-of-freedom method and the primary between-group contrast.

evidence.text: The plan proposes generalized linear mixed-effects models or an alternative approach with demographic covariates but does not specify outcome distribution, effects, covariance or contrast.

requirement: Account for clinic-level confounding and the planned 1:1 matching on age, race, sex or ethnicity, documenting the matching algorithm, caliper or exact factors, unmatched participants, estimand after matching, clinic effect and variance estimation appropriate to the small number of clinics.

evidence.text: The two groups are to be matched 1:1 using characteristics such as race, sex and age across two to three clinics.
The plan adds age, race and ethnicity matching if possible but gives no algorithm or analysis of matched data.

requirement: State the primary estimand with eligible population, video-versus-brochure condition, knowledge-score variable, selected posteducation timepoint, between-group summary measure and handling of nonreceipt, cross-exposure, missed assessments and clinic changes.

evidence.text: The protocol defines education modalities and repeated assessment intent but no estimand or intercurrent-event strategy.

requirement: Prespecify handling of missing questionnaire items, absent immediate or one-month assessments and loss to follow-up, report reasons by education group and clinic, state the primary missing-data assumption and retain partial repeated records through likelihood or justified imputation.

evidence.text: Repeated questionnaires and a one-year enrollment period are described without missing-data rules.
The plan provides no missing-item, missed-visit or dropout method.

requirement: Include sensitivity analyses for unmatched participants, alternative clinic adjustment, telephone versus in-person follow-up and plausible missing-not-at-random knowledge scores, without replacing the prespecified primary matched analysis.

evidence.text: Matching is conditional on feasibility and assessments may span clinics; robustness methods are absent.
Telephone follow-up is allowed and no sensitivity analyses are specified.

requirement: Define decision-making or willingness to seek HCV evaluation and treatment as a separate secondary outcome with its instrument, binary or continuous derivation, assessment time and effect measure; do not conflate it with knowledge retention or HCV seropositivity.

evidence.text: The protocol separately names decision-making capacity and willingness for HCV treatment but gives no operational derivation.

requirement: Treat logistic models of HCV seropositivity and clinic-characteristic associations as exploratory background analyses unless an independently prespecified cohort and endpoint are confirmed; they must not replace the education-effect primary analysis.
acceptable_values: population and outcome confirmed before use

evidence.text: The plan proposes logistic regression for HCV seropositivity as a function of clinic and individual characteristics even though the stated intervention objective is education.

requirement: Protect one prespecified primary education contrast at two-sided alpha 0.05 and define control of multiplicity across immediate and one-month visits, knowledge and decision outcomes, covariates, clinic associations and exploratory models, or label nonprimary analyses exploratory with intervals.

evidence.text: The plan states significance level 0.05 only for its power table and lists multiple outcomes, times and models without a multiplicity strategy.

requirement: Replace or justify the reference plan's 81-per-group calculation before freezing the benchmark: it powers a 20-percentage-point difference in first HCV-evaluation attendance at 80% power and alpha 0.05, not the stated repeated knowledge-score endpoint; derive the prospective target for the adjudicated primary outcome, matching, clinic structure and attrition without substituting actual enrollment.

evidence.text: The plan selects 81 per group for a 20% difference in first HCV-evaluation appointment attendance with 80% power and alpha 0.05, while the study objective centers on knowledge and decision making.

requirement: State sidedness, alpha, confidence level, effect-size scale, model-based interval, degrees-of-freedom or small-sample correction and statistical software for each inferential analysis.

evidence.text: The plan gives alpha 0.05 for the power table but omits sidedness, intervals, effect measures, small-sample inference and software.

requirement: Define proportionate safety and privacy reporting for a minimal-risk behavioral study, including the exposed population, intervention-related distress or disclosure events, serious adverse events if collected, confidentiality breaches and group-specific counts, while avoiding unsupported clinical-safety claims.

evidence.text: The protocol identifies breach of confidentiality as the primary potential risk and describes encrypted, password-protected data handling.

requirement: Use descriptive summaries appropriate to distribution and scale, but prespecify rather than choose mean/SD versus median/IQR or an alternative model solely after viewing outcomes; show baseline balance and post-match balance separately by education group and clinic.

evidence.text: The plan proposes box plots and histograms and means/SD or medians/IQR as appropriate without a selection rule.

requirement: Keep the three-page Statistical Analysis Plan annotation-only and outside every model-visible input; expose only the five-page protocol for protocol-only generation, preserving the exact NCT04204447, title and 2018-06-30 prerecruitment provenance.

evidence.text: The protocol cover prints NCT04204447, the study title, document type and 2018-06-30 date.
The separate plan cover prints the same NCT, title and date and is an annotation aid rather than model input.
